title: The duplicate check read the clone's stale origin/main and a shallow 14-day window
problem: CLAUDE.md said to search open PRs and recent main commits only before opening a PR, and slug_dupe.py grepped whatever origin/main the clone held. A cloud clone's ref is hours old by the time a run builds, so a sibling that merged in the meantime is invisible, and in a shallow clone the --days 14 log grep covered only the commits the clone happened to have.
evidence: prompts/runs/2026-11-25-session_01AcxTtGdNyP3tnH67NWocLz.json doc_friction: the local origin/main was hours stale and the duplicate (#18769) had merged in the meantime; the same run's venture-preflight said 'this branch edits platform/ci' because of the stale ref
2026-11-25, this session: `slug_dupe.py job-shop` refreshed HEAD + origin/main from 890 to 4322 commits (back to 2026-11-11), so the 14-day window had been about 1 day deep in a fresh clone
change: slug_dupe.py refreshes <remote>/main with fetch_ref.py (keeping --days of history) before checking; --no-fetch skips it; a failed fetch warns and reads the local ref. CLAUDE.md 'Duplicate PRs' and duplicate-work.md name it at task pick and before the PR.
metric: Run records from the following 7 days whose doc_friction or notes report a duplicate found only after building, or a stale origin/main misreading
baseline: 2026-11-23..25: 2 sessions in friction_rank cluster #19 (stale ref), plus the duplicate pairs named in duplicate-work.md

history.note: Shipped. Refresh costs about 7 s once history is present; the first call in a fresh clone fetches 14 days of main.
